meta.originalInput: Notice how you try to force concentration the second your mind begins to wander. You believe focus is an act of sheer willpower, but cognitive neuroscience proves it is an act of aggressive elimination. When you fight distraction directly, you feed the exact neural loops that scatter your attention. Strip the friction. Close the secondary tabs. Clear the room. Focus isn't something you force into existence. Focus is simply what remains when everything else is gone.
